disputed: President Trump initially denied the US had struck the school and, as of the Human Rights Watch report, had said he did not know about the Pentagon's own preliminary findings suggesting otherwise. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Hegseth both said the US does not deliberately target civilian infrastructure and stated an investigation was underway; as of the UN report (Sept. 2026), no final US investigative conclusion had been made public. Rubio alleged Iranian forces have targeted civilian infrastructure including airports, hotels and embassies. Death-toll figures vary by source (150-186) and Reuters said it could not independently confirm Iran's figures. Iran did not grant UN investigators access, and only responded to about a quarter of the UN's information requests; Israel's government did not respond to the UN's requests either.

items: Two missile strikes in quick succession hit the Shajareh Tayyebeh ('The Good Tree') girls' primary school in Minab, southern Iran, on the war's first day, killing at least 168-186 people (Iranian state media/officials), most of them girls aged 7-12. US military investigators told Reuters (March 2026) it was likely US forces were responsible, though the investigation was not complete; independent investigations by Al Jazeera and Amnesty International said the attack was likely deliberate and probably used a US-made Tomahawk missile. Trump publicly denied US responsibility at the time. (Al Jazeera; Reuters via Malay Mail; HRW)

Human Rights Watch found no evidence the school was used for military purposes and said even a nearby legitimate military target would not justify an attack expected to cause disproportionate civilian harm; it asked the US and Israeli militaries (March 2) and Iranian authorities (March 3) for information and called for a war-crimes investigation. (HRW)
sections.label: The Minab school strike (Feb. 28, 2026)

items: A UN-backed international fact-finding mission found 'reasonable grounds to believe the United States committed the war crime of launching indiscriminate attacks resulting in the loss of life or injury to civilians' in both the Minab school strike (168+ deaths, per Iranian state media) and a second US strike the same day on a sports center and residential area in Lamerd that killed 22 civilians. The mission separately found Iranian security forces committed 'gross human rights violations and crimes against humanity' through 'violent repression' of protesters over the prior two years. (CNN; NPR/AP)

The US State Department did not immediately respond to AP's request for comment on the UN findings. Reporting also noted the Trump administration had cut about 90% of Defense Department teams responsible for reducing civilian casualties in military operations, and outdated targeting information reportedly contributed to the strike. (NPR/AP; CFR)
sections.label: UN fact-finding mission findings (Sept. 2026)

items: On March 28, 2026, the Iran University of Science and Technology was hit in what Iranian media described as targeted Israeli-US strikes; a day later a university in Isfahan was hit for a second time, wounding four staff. The IRGC said afterward it would retaliate against universities tied to the US and Israel across the Middle East. (Al Jazeera)

Humanitarian organizations, including the International Federation for Human Rights, called for investigation into attacks on schools and hospitals, saying international law requires 'alleged violations -- including indiscriminate or disproportionate attacks, deliberate targeting of civilians or civilian infrastructure, and attacks on medical facilities and schools' to be 'promptly, independently, and transparently investigated.' Total reported deaths across the region by early in the war included more than 1,300 in Iran, at least 570 in Lebanon, 15 in Israel, and additional deaths across Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. (Yahoo/ABC News; CFR)
sections.label: University strikes and broader civilian-target pattern

summary: On Feb. 28, 2026, the first day of the US-Israeli war on Iran ('Operation Epic Fury'), missiles hit a girls' primary school in Minab, killing at least 168-186 people, most of them children, and a second strike hit a sports center/residential area in Lamerd, killing 22 civilians. US military investigators found it likely US forces were responsible; a UN fact-finding mission later found reasonable grounds that the US committed the war crime of launching indiscriminate attacks in both strikes. Iranian universities were also struck in the following weeks.
title: US-Israeli strikes on an Iranian school, university and civilian sites; UN war-crimes findings
